scope: Review of the supplied fictional design only; no runtime execution or production access.
summary: The design retries non-idempotent increments after ambiguous timeouts. Authorization enforcement is unspecified and needs investigation before any claim that it is absent.
assumptions: This example is invented and contains no customer or production data.
limitations: Coverage is limited to retries and authorization; other domains are not assessed.

artifacts.label: Synthetic design excerpt
artifacts.basis: Fictional supplied specification: adjust_stock increments on every POST, accepts no duplicate key, and may commit before response loss. The worker repeats the POST after timeout, up to three attempts. Authorization behaviour is not described.

sources.claim: Retrying operations with side effects requires considering duplicates and idempotent request semantics.

findings.title: Timeout retries can repeat a stock increment
findings.mechanism: The documented worker repeats a non-idempotent POST after timeout, although the service contract allows commit before response loss.
findings.impact: Repeated increment in the fictional inventory workflow; business value and real-world deployment are not assessed.
findings.severity_rationale: A bounded state-integrity defect within the described synthetic design; no evidence of broader exposure.
findings.likelihood_rationale: The documented path is reachable on response loss; operational frequency is unknown.

evidence.observation: Every POST increments state, and the worker retries timeouts without duplicate suppression.

findings.title: Authorization boundary is not evidenced
findings.mechanism: The design does not specify identity propagation or the enforcement point; no bypass is established.
findings.impact: Cannot assess unauthorized-action exposure without the actual policy and execution contract.
findings.likelihood_rationale: Unknown; no operational evidence or demonstrated bypass.

evidence.observation: Authorization is not described in this supplied excerpt.

missing_evidence: Executor authorization implementation, delegation model and negative-test evidence.

action_items.change: Add durable operation IDs and atomic duplicate detection tied to the stock update; persist the ID before dispatch. Define reconciliation for unknown outcomes before enabling retries.
action_items.rationale: Repeated delivery of the same logical operation must not repeat its state change.
action_items.tradeoffs: Adds storage, concurrency handling and an operation-retention policy; requires endpoint support.
action_items.failure_behavior: On unavailable deduplication storage or conflicting ID payload, do not issue an unchecked increment; record a pending/error state.
action_items.recovery: Reconcile pending operation IDs against committed inventory changes in an authorized isolated test before defining production repair.
action_items.residual_risk: Independent downstream side effects are not made atomic by this control; key lifetime and backup restoration require separate review.

action_items.change: Inspect the actual executor and permission model before proposing new access-control components.
action_items.rationale: Resolve the evidence gap without claiming an existing control is absent.
action_items.tradeoffs: Requires implementation access; a design excerpt alone cannot complete this check.
action_items.failure_behavior: Keep authorization conclusions unresolved if implementation evidence remains unavailable.
action_items.recovery: No state-changing investigation is proposed; preserve collected artifact provenance.
action_items.residual_risk: Inspection may not establish runtime enforcement; controlled negative tests remain necessary.

tests.setup: Isolated stock service and worker with synthetic state and durable operation store.
tests.stimulus: Commit an increment, drop the response, then retry with the same operation ID; also submit the same ID concurrently and with different parameters.
tests.expected: One logical increment; duplicates return the established result and conflicting parameters are rejected; pending outcome is reconciled.
tests.collect: Before/after stock state, operation record, actual execution count and retry trace.

tests.setup: Authorized inspection plus an isolated executor with synthetic resource permissions.
tests.stimulus: Trace the policy check and attempt an unauthorized resource/action request in the isolated environment.
tests.expected: Identify the actual execution-boundary control and obtain denial evidence, or report the observed defect with its exact scope.
tests.collect: Implementation location, authorization result and proof that denied requests cause no state change.

validated_controls.description: The fictional design bounds timeout retries to three attempts.
validated_controls.boundary: Design statement only; does not establish duplicate safety or deployed retry behaviour.

evidence.observation: A maximum of three attempts is specified.

coverage.reason: Endpoint and worker contracts supplied in the fictional excerpt.
Executor identity and enforcement are unspecified.
